question: Where is the LPT shaft bolted to the LPT assembly?

options.b: At the LPT rotor disk stage 6
options.c: To the front of the fan disk

justification: States: 'The shaft is bolted to the LPT at the LPT rotor disk stage 6 and extends forward through the engine.'

question: What provides the inner contour of the common exhaust stream flow?
justification: States: 'The exhaust cone supplies the inner contour of the common exhaust stream flow.'

question: What is the role of the angle gearbox in the AGB assembly?

options.a: To separate oil and air from the bearing compartments
options.b: To transmit power from the engine to the main gearbox and from the starter to the engine
options.c: To control the pitch of the fan blades

justification: States: 'The angle gearbox transmits power from the engine to the main gearbox and from the starter on the main gearbox to the engine.'

question: Which component is NOT driven by the main gearbox?
justification: /Diagram shows IDG and Fuel pumps are driven by the gearbox. The P2/T2 probe is a sensor on the inlet cowl ().

question: How does the oil pressure pump receive its movement?

options.b: Through the fuel pump drive gearshaft
options.c: By an electric motor controlled by the EEC

justification: States: 'The oil pressure pump receives the movement through the fuel pump drive gearshaft...'

question: What is the function of the deoiler?

options.a: To separate air and oil by centrifugal action
options.b: To remove moisture from the bleed air system
options.c: To cool the IDG oil using fuel

justification: States: 'The deoiler receives the movement through the Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) system gearshaft and separates air and oil by centrifugal action.'

question: Where is deaerated oil from the deoiler sent?
justification: States: 'The deaerated oil goes back to the oil system and the clean air is bled overboard.'

question: What warning is given regarding the removal of the IDG from the gearbox?

options.a: The engine must be shut down for at least 5 minutes to prevent burns
options.b: A 24V DC battery must be connected to maintain the EEC memory
options.c: The thrust reverser must be in the deployed position

justification: States: 'Before removing the IDG, the engine must be shut down for at least 5 minutes to prevent burns because the oil stays hot...'

question: During IDG installation, what is the significance of the square washers?

options.a: They seal the oil tubes to prevent leaks
options.b: They are installed between phase cables and the terminal block to prevent overheating
options.c: They are used to align the splined drive shaft

justification: States: 'The square washers must be installed between the phase cables and the terminal block on the IDG to prevent the terminal block becoming hot and causing damage to the IDG.'

question: What caution is provided when pulling the IDG from the gearbox?

options.a: Help the IDG out in a straight line so the input shaft does not catch the seal
options.b: Ensure the oil tank is at the 'FULL' mark
options.c: Rotate the fan clockwise to disengage the internal gears

justification: States: 'Help the IDG out in a straight line, the input shaft can catch and cause damage to the input seal. Do not use external parts or tools to pull the IDG...'

question: During IDG servicing, why must the drain hose be connected to the overflow drain valve?

options.a: To allow air to escape and oil to flow around the system
options.b: To bypass the main scavenge filter
options.c: To maintain N1 speed at exactly 20%

justification: States: 'NOTE: This procedure is to let the air escape from the IDG oil system and to let the oil flow around the system.'

question: A technician is adding oil to the IDG. At what point should they stop adding oil?

options.a: When the ECAM oil quantity reaches 14.0 quarts
options.b: Until it overflows through the drain hose, then drain until the level is in the green band
options.c: When the pressure fill valve reaches 450 PSI

justification: States: 'Using the service units, add oil, until the level reaches the full mark and the oil overflows through the drain hose. Drain oil until the oil level moves down to the green band.'

question: The Full Authority Digital Engine Control (FADEC) system consists of:

options.a: A single-channel EEC and a mechanical backup
options.b: A dual-channel EEC and its peripheral components and sensors
options.c: Three independent computers located in the avionics bay

justification: States: 'It [FADEC] consists of a dual channel Electronic Engine Control (EEC) and its peripheral components and sensors.'

question: What are the two primary parameters sent directly by the EEC to the ECAM?

options.c: Hydraulic pressure and Landing Gear status

justification: States: 'The primary parameters Engine Pressure Ratio (EPR), Low Pressure Rotor Speed (N1)... are sent directly by the EEC to the ECAM.'

question: What is the power source for the FADEC system when N2 is greater than 10%?

options.c: 115 VAC from the Integrated Drive Generator

justification: States: 'The FADEC system is self-powered by a dedicated Permanent Magnet Alternator (PMA) when N2 is greater than 10%.'

question: In the event of a single output signal failure in the FADEC, what action is taken?

options.a: The engine immediately reverts to N1 unrated mode
options.b: There is an automatic switchover to the standby active channel
options.c: The EEC behaves as if there is a dual input signal failure

justification: States: '- single output signal failure, there is an automatic switchover to the standby active channel.'

question: What happens if both channels of the FADEC lose control functions for a component?

options.a: The component remains in its last known position
options.b: The component moves to a fail-safe position
options.c: The engine automatically executes a shutdown

justification: States: 'In the event of loss of control functions on both channels, each servo valve and actuator has a fail-safe position.'

question: A technician needs to perform maintenance tests on the EEC while the engine is shut down. How can the EEC be powered on the ground?

options.a: By rotating the fan manually to 10% N2
options.b: By using the ENGine FADEC GrouND PoWeR pushbutton switch
options.c: By setting the engine MASTER lever to ON and the fuel pumps to OFF

justification: States: '...the ENGine FADEC GrouND PoWeR panel permits FADEC power supply to be restored on the ground with engines shut down. When the corresponding... P/B is pressed ON the EEC recovers its power supply.'

question: Which aircraft computer acts as an interface concentrator between airframe systems and the FADEC?
justification: States: '...the EEC interfaces with A/C computers... via the Engine Interface Unit (EIU), which is an interface concentrator between the A/C systems and the FADEC system.'

question: If a technician is checking FADEC depowering, after how long will the system automatically depower after engine shutdown on the ground?
justification: States: 'EEC automatic depowering occurs on the ground... 5 min after engine shutdown.'

question: What is the effect on engine control if the EIU fails entirely?

options.a: The FADEC power supply is cut off immediately
options.b: The power supply for FADEC and ignition is preserved (fail safe position)
options.c: The engine will automatically surge due to loss of VSV control

justification: States: 'NOTE: Note: In case of EIU failure, the power supply for FADEC and ignition is preserved (fail safe position).'

question: During a manual engine start, which signal allows the ignition system to be energized?

options.a: The ENG MAN START P/B being pressed
options.b: The MASTER control lever being set to the ON position

justification: States: 'During a manual start... then the ignition system is energized when the MASTER control lever is set to the ON position.'

question: On the ECAM EPR indicator, what does the white circle represent?

options.b: The predicted EPR determined by the TLA
options.c: The EPR limit computed by the EEC

justification: States: 'The predicted Engine Pressure Ratio (EPR) is indicated by a white circle on the EPR indicator and corresponds to the value determined by the Throttle Resolver Angle (TRA).'

question: What does a green needle and digital indication on the EPR dial represent?
justification: States: 'The actual EPR is displayed in green on the EPR indicator.'

question: What is the source of the engine vibration signals monitored by the EVMU?

options.a: Single accelerometer located on the exhaust case
options.b: A dual accelerometer installed on each engine
options.c: Proximity sensors on the HP turbine shaft

justification: States: 'A dual accelerometer is installed on each engine. It provides the analog signals of N1 and N2 vibration frequencies.'

question: How many N1 speed sensors are installed in the front bearing compartment?
justification: States: 'The fan speed (N1) indicating system has 4 sensors... installed on the front brackets attached to the No. 2 bearing support...'

question: What is the conversion factor for N1/N2 vibration units to Inches Per Second (IPS)?
justification: States: '1 unit for N1 or N2 rotor corresponds to 0.3IPS (Inch Per Second).'

question: If an EPR sensor (P2 or P4.9) fails, how does the EEC respond?

options.a: It commands a shutdown to protect the engine
options.b: It automatically reverts to the rated N1 mode
options.c: It switches to using the other engine's EPR data

justification: States: 'In case of EPR sensor failure, i.e. P2 or P4.9, the EEC automatically reverts to the rated N1 mode.'

question: What indication appears on the ECAM if an N1 rated mode is forced by pressing the N1 MODE pushbuttons?

options.a: The EPR indicator is crossed amber
options.b: The EGT digital value flashes green
options.c: A red 'NO EPR' warning appears on the EWD

justification: States: 'When the N1 MODE P/Bs are pressed in... On the ECAM, the EPR indicator is crossed amber and the N1 MODE limit is displayed...'

question: What is the significance of the unrated N1 mode regarding engine protection?

options.a: There is no longer engine protection against over boost (e.g. Go-Around)
options.b: The overspeed protection for N2 is disabled
options.c: The fire detection loops are automatically inhibited

justification: States: 'NOTE: in unrated N1 mode, there is no longer an engine protection against over boost, e.g. Go-Around.'

question: Where is the engine EGT sensed and how many probe assemblies are used?

options.b: Sensed and averaged by 4 thermocouple probe assemblies at station 4.95
options.c: Sensed by 20 nozzles at the exit of the combustion chamber

justification: States: 'The engine EGT is sensed and averaged by 4 thermocouple probe assemblies are located at station 4.95 (LP turbine exhaust case strut).'

question: In case of a vibration sensor failure, how is the transfer to the second sensor (A to B) handled?

options.a: Automatically by the EEC in flight
options.b: Carried out on the ground through the MCDU
options.c: By cycling the engine MASTER lever

justification: States: 'NOTE: In case of sensor failure, the transfer to the second sensor is carried out on the ground through the MCDU.'

question: What provides engine oil cooling and Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) oil cooling?

options.a: Engine fuel through various heat exchangers
options.b: Hydraulic fluid from the green system

justification: States: 'The engine fuel system is designed to provide... cooling for engine oil and Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) oil.'

question: Which unit is responsible for metering fuel flow into the combustion chamber?
justification: And 97 identify the FMU as containing the fuel metering valve used to regulate fuel flow to the nozzles.

question: What happens if the fuel filter in the Fuel Cooled Oil Cooler (FCOC) becomes clogged?

options.a: The engine will surge and automatically shut down
options.b: A bypass valve opens to ensure fuel still flows to the engine
options.c: The FMU shuts off the fuel supply to prevent contamination

justification: States: 'The fuel filter bypass valve makes sure that the fuel still flow in the event of fuel filter clogging.'

question: The Fuel Distribution Valve (FDV) supplies fuel to:
justification: States: 'The ten discharge ports are connected to the ten fuel manifolds, each of which in turn supplies two nozzles (20 nozzles at all).'

question: What is the purpose of the two fuel manifolds that remain full after engine shutdown?

options.a: To provide lubrication for the LPT shaft
options.b: To help supply fuel for the next engine start
options.c: To maintain pressure in the high pressure pump

justification: States: 'The two fuel manifolds, which remain full, help to supply fuel for the next engine start.'

question: In 'Mode 1' of the Heat Management System, how is fuel returned to the tank?

options.a: When the engine is at high power, the return valve is fully open
options.b: When the engine is NOT at high power setting, some fuel is returned to the tank
options.c: Only when the IDG oil temperature exceeds 165°C

justification: For Mode 1: 'When the engine is not at high power setting, some of the fuel is returned to the tank.'

question: Which Heat Management System mode is considered the 'fail-safe' mode?
justification: Identifies Mode 5 as the 'fail-safe mode of operation' where the ACOC valve is fully open.

question: What allows an aircraft to be dispatched per MEL if the ECAM 'FUEL CLOG' warning fails?

options.a: The fuel filter must be changed once each day
options.b: The engine must only be operated at minimum idle
options.c: The ACOC modulating valve must be locked open

justification: States: 'In case of a failure of the FUEL CLOG warning on ECAM, the aircraft may be dispatched per MEL as long as the fuel filter is changed once each day.'

question: During engine shutdown, which component is primarily responsible for stopping fuel flow to the combustion chamber?

options.b: The Pressure Raising and Shut Off Valve (PRSOV)

justification: States: 'When the Master switch is set from On to OFF... The PRSOV closes and the fuel flow to the Fuel Distribution Valve and the combustion chamber is stopped.'

question: How is the LP Fuel Shut-Off Valve (SOV) controlled to close when the Master Switch is set to OFF?

options.a: By a mechanical cable from the center pedestal
options.b: By an electrical signal sent to the two motors of the LP Valve
options.c: By the reduction in hydraulic system pressure

justification: States: 'A second electrical signal is sent to the two motors of the LP Valve, which is controlled to close...'

question: What are the main components of the pneumatic starting system on the IAE V2500?

options.a: An electric starter motor and a backup battery
options.b: A starter valve and a pneumatic starter
options.c: A hydraulic motor and a high-pressure accumulator

justification: The start system is made up of the start valve and the starter (pneumatic).

question: Where is the start valve manual override located for maintenance operation on the ground?

options.b: On the Electronic Engine Control (EEC) front panel

justification: And 152 indicate that the starter valve is fitted with a manual override for mechanic operation on the ground.

question: During an automatic start sequence, at what N2 speed does the EEC close the starter valve and cut off the ignition?
justification: And 160 state: 'When N2 reaches 43%, the EEC closes the starter valve and cuts off the ignition.'

question: In manual start mode, what action causes the starter valve to open?

options.a: Moving the Master lever to ON
options.b: Pressing the ENG MAN START P/B
options.c: Setting the Mode selector to IGN START

justification: States: 'Action on the ENG MANual START P/B opens the starter valve, via the EEC.'

question: What is the primary difference in EEC protection between automatic and manual start modes?

options.a: Manual mode provides higher EGT limits than automatic mode
options.b: There is no automatic shutdown function in manual mode
options.c: Ignition is inhibited during the first 30 seconds of an automatic start

justification: And 169 explicitly state: 'NOTE: there is no automatic shutdown function in manual mode/start.'

question: During a manual engine start, how long should the engine be dry cranked before setting the ENG/MASTER switch to ON?
justification: States: 'After 30 seconds dry crank, set the ENG/MASTER control switch to ON.'

question: Which component converts the 115V AC from the EEC/Relay Box into high-energy pulses for the igniter plugs?
justification: The warning states: 'THE EEC AND THE RELAY BOX SEND 115 VOLTS TO THE IGNITION BOXES, WHICH CONVERT IT AND SEND HIGH ENERGY PULSES THROUGH THE IGNITION LEADS TO THE IGNITERS PLUGS.'

question: If the second engine is being started, what is the required position for the ENG MODE selector according to the manual?

options.a: Move it to NORM then back to IGN START
options.b: Leave the selector in the IGN START position

justification: States: 'NOTE: to start the second engine, you leave the MODE selector in the IGN START position, and set the MASTER lever... to ON.'

question: What is the maximum duration for a manual engine start attempt?
justification: States: 'In case of malfunction, set the MASTER lever in the OFF position to abort the start. Start for up to 2 minutes maximum.'

question: During an automatic start, what initiates the opening of the Pressure Raising and Shut-Off Valve (PRSOV)?

options.a: A mechanical linkage from the starter valve
options.b: Fuel pressure from the Fuel Metering Valve (FMV) provided its torque motor is de-energized
options.c: Hydraulic pressure from the Green system

justification: States: '...the EEC controls the opening of the Fuel Metering Valve (FMV), which causes the pressure raising and SOV to open, provided its latching torque motor is de-energized....[It] will only open if fuel pressure from the FMV is available.'

question: What is inhibited when the ENG MODE selector is in the CRANK position?

options.a: Hydraulic supply to the thrust reverser

justification: States: 'When CRANK is selected on the ground, the ignition is inhibited.'

question: What are the two types of engine cranking sequences described in the manual?

options.a: Low speed and high speed cranking

justification: States: 'Engine motoring could be performed for dry cranking or wet cranking sequences.'

question: During a wet crank, at what N2 percentage should the MASTER lever be set to ON?
justification: States: 'To perform a wet crank, allow N2 to increase to 20% RPM before setting the MASTER lever to ON.'

question: What is the purpose of dry cranking after a wet crank sequence has been performed?

options.b: To eliminate fuel vapors from the engine
options.c: To lubricate the N2 shaft bearings

justification: States: 'After wet cranking, the MASTER lever should be set to OFF, and dry cranking will continue to eliminate fuel vapors from the engine.'

question: Which valve remains closed during a dry crank sequence to prevent fuel from entering the engine?

options.b: The Pressure Raising and Shut-Off Valve (PRSOV)

justification: States: 'The pressure raising and SOV is closed [during dry crank].'

question: What are the starter limitations for a dry crank consisting of three consecutive cycles?

options.b: 2 minutes on, 15 seconds off (up to 2 times), then 1 minute on and 30 minutes off

justification: States: 'The starter limitations... a maximum of 3 consecutive cycles; 2 minutes on, 15 seconds off up 2 times and one minute on, then 30 minutes off for cooling.'

question: If a technician performs a continuous dry crank, what is the maximum time allowed before a 30-minute cooling period is required?
justification: States: '...or 4 continuous minutes on, then 30 minutes off for cooling.'

question: What happens if the starter operation time limit is exceeded during a crank sequence?

options.a: The FADEC automatically aborts the sequence
options.b: A warning message is displayed on the ECAM, but there is no automatic abort
options.c: The air starter motor is automatically disconnected by a shear pin

justification: States: 'If the starter operation time is exceeded, a warning message is displayed on the ECAM, but there is no automatic abort.'

question: How long must an engine continue to dry crank after a wet crank to safely eliminate fuel vapors?
justification: States: 'After wet cranking... Continue to dry crank for at least 60 seconds.'

question: To finish a crank sequence, what is the final step for the cockpit control?

options.a: Move the MASTER lever to ON
options.b: Set the ENG MODE selector to NORM
options.c: Release the ENG MAN START P/B and leave the selector in CRANK

justification: States: 'To complete the crank sequence the MODE selector is set in the NORM position.'

question: Which lights illuminate on the engine panel if a 'Start Valve Not Open' fault is detected?

options.b: MASTER CAUT and ENG FAULT lights

justification: States: 'If the start valve does not open... The MASTER CAUTion and the ENGine FAULT lights come on.'

question: What indication is given to the crew if a disagreement is detected between start valve control and position?

options.a: A steady blue light on the overhead maintenance panel
options.b: An ECAM warning and the illumination of the FAULT light
options.c: The N2 display turns red on the EWD

justification: (regarding PRSOV/Start Valve monitoring) and confirm: 'In case of disagreement... an ECAM warning is triggered and the FAULT light comes on.'

question: If an ignition fault occurs during automatic start mode, what is the FADEC's immediate response?

options.a: It switches to the other ignition channel and continues
options.b: It stops fuel supply and ignition, and automatically supplies ventilation (airflow)
options.c: It locks the thrust reverser in the deployed position

justification: States: 'If an ignition fault occurs... The FADEC stops the fuel supply and ignition, and automatically supplies airflow to the engine.'

question: What happens if a stall or EGT overlimit is sensed during an automatic start?

options.a: The engine enters N1 unrated mode
options.b: The FADEC stops fuel/ignition and performs an automatic dry crank phase
options.c: The EEC increases fuel flow to blow out the stall

justification: States: 'When a stall or an EGT overlimit is sensed... The FADEC stops the fuel and the ignition, then a dry crank phase is automatically done.'

question: If the start valve does not close at 43% N2, what must the technician remove to isolate the valve?

options.b: All bleed sources that supply the faulty start valve

justification: States: 'For this [Start Valve Not Closed], you must remove all bleed sources that supply the faulty start valve.'

question: In the case of a 'Start Valve Not Open' failure, at what N2 speed should the ground crew be instructed to manually close the start valve?
justification: States: 'When N2 is at 43%, tell the ground crew to close the start valve.'

question: A technician is performing a manual start and observes an EGT exceedance. Does the FADEC abort the start?

options.a: Yes, it aborts automatically above 50% N2
options.b: No, the Crew must operate the MASTER LEVER switch to OFF to stop the engine
options.c: Yes, but only if the ENG MAN START P/B is still pressed

justification: States: 'In manual start, the FADEC does not abort the start. The Crew operates the MASTER LEVER switch to OFF to stop the engine...'

question: During a 'Start Valve Not Closed' procedure, what is the required position for the X BLEED selector?
justification: States: 'Set the X BLEED selector to SHUT' as part of the procedure to remove bleed sources.

question: If an automatic start sequence is aborted due to a failure, at what N2 speed is the abort capability typically limited?
justification: And 89 state that the start sequence can be aborted (e.g. by EEC) below 50% N2.

question: Following a 'Start Valve Not Closed' event and the completion of the cockpit procedure, what is the dispatch status?

options.a: Aircraft can be dispatched per MEL with valve locked open
options.b: Restart is not permitted, and a maintenance procedure is necessary
options.c: The engine can be restarted once EGT is below 100°C

justification: Explicitly states: 'Restart is not permitted, and a maintenance procedure is necessary.'

question: Which system is used to prevent blade stall and engine surge in the initial stages of the HPC?
justification: States: 'The VSV system directs the airflow into the HPC 4 initial stages to prevent blade stall and engine surge.'

question: Where are the High Pressure Compressor (HPC) additional bleed valves located?
justification: And 246 state there are bleed valves at the 7th and 10th stages of the HPC.

question: The Booster Stage Bleed Valve (BSBV) is controlled by the EEC to be:

options.a: Either fully open or fully closed only (two-position)
options.b: Fully modulating between open and closed

justification: States: 'The bleed valve is controlled by the EEC and is fully modulating, between the fully open and the fully closed positions.'

question: How many handling bleed valves are used on the 7th stage of the HPC?
justification: And 246 state: '...three for the 7th stage and one for the 10th stage of the HPC...'

question: What is the physical configuration of the Booster Stage Bleed Valve (BSBV)?

options.a: A series of twenty butterfly valves
options.b: A continuous ring valve that rotates and slides

justification: States: 'The BSBV is a continuous ring valve that rotates and slides forward to open and rearwards to close.'

question: What is the default (spring-loaded) position of the handling bleed valves for engine start?
justification: States: 'All the bleed valves are spring loaded to the open position and as a result will always be in the correct position (open) for starting.'

question: Which BSBV actuator provides positional feedback to the EEC through an LVDT?
justification: States: 'Only the left actuator interfaces with the EEC... identified as the Master Actuator... The Master Actuator includes a LVDT, which transmits the actuator position... to the EEC.'

question: What hydraulic medium is used to operate the BSBV actuators?
justification: States: 'The two [BSBV] actuators use the high-pressure fuel from the FMU as a hydraulic medium.'

question: During engine acceleration, how does the EEC close the handling bleed valves?

options.a: By de-energizing the solenoid to apply spring pressure
options.b: By energizing the solenoid control valve to vent P3 servo air

justification: States: 'The EEC will close the bleed valves... [by energizing] the solenoid control valve... [which] vents the P3 servo air from the opening chamber... and the valve will move to the closed position.'

question: When does the BSBV reach its fully closed position?
justification: States: '...while during cruise and take off the valve is fully closed.'

question: The Variable Stator Vane (VSV) system controls the air entry into which stages of the HPC?
justification: States: 'The variable vanes control the angle at which the air enters the first three stages of the H.P. compressor.'

question: How many unison rings are used in the VSV system mechanical arrangement?
justification: States: 'Short rods to a crankshaft connect the five unison rings.'

question: What parameter is used to determine the angle variation of the VSVs?
justification: States: 'The angle varies with the H.P. compressor speed (N2); this reduces the risk of blade stall and compressor surge.'

question: The VSV system includes Inlet Guide Vanes (IGVs) located in front of stage:
justification: States: 'The four stages of variable vanes comprises Inlet Guide Vanes (IGVs) in front of stage 3...'

question: What prevents failure propagation in the VSV actuation signal?

options.a: Mechanical redundancy of the unison rings
options.b: LVDT positional feedback to the EEC
options.c: The use of a backup electric motor

justification: States: 'The actuator has an LVDT, which sends actuator positional information back to the EEC.' This closed-loop control allows for fault detection.

question: If the EEC is unable to control the VSV position, what is the fail-safe state of the vanes?
justification: States: '...unable to control the Variable Stator Vane (VSV) position, the vanes are set to the fail-safe open position.'

question: Where are the VSVs (Variable Stator Vanes) located relative to the stages?
justification: States: '...and the Variable Stator Vanes (VSVs) behind the stages 3, 4, and 5.'

question: What mechanical component connects the crankshaft to the unison rings?
justification: States: 'Short rods to a crankshaft connect the five unison rings.'

question: What medium is used as the hydraulic operating medium for the VSV actuator?
justification: States: 'A short rod to an actuator that uses H.P. fuel as a hydraulic operating medium connects the crankshaft.'

question: How is each vane pivoted to allow rotation?

options.a: At its inner and outer ends
options.b: Only at the outer end near the unison ring
options.c: Fixed at the inner end and pivoted at the center

justification: States: 'Each vane has pivots at its inner and outer ends, which allow the vane to rotate about its longitudinal axis.'

question: What is the purpose of the Active Clearance Control (ACC) system?

options.a: To control the fuel flow into the burner
options.b: To control the tip clearances of the turbines for better performance
options.c: To manage the bleed air for the environmental control system

justification: And 254 state: 'The ACC system fulfills the blade tip clearances of the turbines for better performance.'

question: What cooling medium does the ACC system use to cool the turbine cases?
justification: States: 'The EEC controls a dual ACC valve, which discharges fan air through manifolds to cool the surfaces of the HP and LP turbine cases...'

question: During which flight phases is fan air typically discharged to cool the turbine cases?
justification: States: '...to cool the surfaces of the HP and LP turbine cases during climb and cruise power operations.'

question: Which input signals are monitored by the EEC to control the opening and closing of the ACC system?
justification: States: 'The EEC controls the opening and closing of the ACC system by monitoring input signals of:. Corrected N2. Altitude'

question: What is the function of the 'Continuous Flow Adapter' in the ACC system?

options.a: To provide continuous lubrication to the gearboxes
options.b: To supply supplemental air from the HPC 10th stage to cool stage 2 blades and HP 1 disc bore
options.c: To vent the oil tank scupper overboard

justification: States: 'The continuous flow adapter supplies supplemental air, from the HPC 10th stage, to cool the stage 2 blades and HP 1 turbine disc bore.'

question: What component in the ACC actuator allows the jet pipe to return to a central position when stabilisation is required?

options.a: The EEC cancelling the input signal to the torque motor
options.b: Mechanical stops on the manifold tubes
options.c: A loss of P10 servo air

justification: States: 'When stabilisation of the piston is required the EEC will cancel the input signal to the torque motor. This allows the jet pipe to return to the central position...'

question: How is the actual movement of the ACC modulating air control valve achieved?

options.b: By the movement of a piston driven by differential servo fuel pressure
options.c: By thermal expansion of the pylon mount bolts

justification: States: 'The pilot valve moves and gets servo fuel pressure to either side of the piston... The movement of the piston moves a push pull rod that in turn operates the modulating air control valve.'

question: What is the role of the dual track LVDTs in the ACC system?

options.a: To sense the temperature of the turbine manifold
options.b: To send feedback signals to the EEC of the ACC system operation
options.c: To provide power to the torque motor

justification: States: 'The dual track LVDTs will send feedback signals to the EEC of the ACC system operation.'

question: How is the No. 4 bearing compartment cooled?

options.a: By fan air through an air-cooled air cooler and 12th stage air of the HPC
options.b: By fuel from the Fuel Cooled Oil Cooler
options.c: By environmental control system bleed air

justification: States: 'The number 4 bearing compartment is cooled by 12th stage air of the HPC... through an air-cooled air cooler... [which] cools the 12th stage air of the HPC with fan air before going into the Nº4 bearing compartment.'

question: According to the ACC valve position graph, which condition corresponds to a fully retracted piston (100%)?
justification: The graph shows that at 100% Piston Travel (Retracted), the valve position is 'E' (Top of Descent / Cruise).

question: What is the purpose of Zone 1 ventilation?

options.a: To cool the HP turbine blades
options.b: To cool the fan case and accessories

justification: States: 'Zone 1: the fan case and accessories are cooled by air taken in by a scoop on the upper side of the air intake cowl.'

question: Where is the nacelle temperature sensor located?

options.a: In the air intake cowl lip

justification: States: 'The nacelle temperature is monitored by a temperature probe installed in the ventilated core compartment.'

question: How is core compartment ventilation (Zone 2) supplied?

options.a: By air taken in by a scoop on the pylon
options.b: By fan air through holes in the inner wall of the thrust reverser 'C' ducts
options.c: By bleed air from the 10th stage of the HPC

justification: States: 'Zone 2: core compartment ventilation is supplied by fan air through holes in the inner wall of the thrust reverser "C" ducts.'

question: Where is the air from Zone 1 ventilation eventually vented overboard?

options.b: Through two ventilation grilles at the bottom of each fan cowl door

justification: States: 'The air is then vented overboard through two ventilation grilles at the bottom of each fan cowl door.'

question: The air in Zone 2 circulates through the core compartment and exits via the:
justification: States: 'The air circulates into the core compartment and flows through the lower bifurcation... then exits through the thrust recovery nozzle.'

question: Which component is used to monitor for over-temperature conditions within the nacelle core?

options.b: The nacelle temperature sensor providing indication to the ECAM lower display

justification: States: 'The nacelle temperature is monitored by a temperature probe... gives indication to the ECAM lower display.' This allows for detecting core zone heat issues.

question: What provides the inlet for Zone 1 cooling air?

options.a: A scoop on the upper side of the air intake cowl

justification: States: 'Zone 1... cooled by air taken in by a scoop on the upper side of the air intake cowl.'

question: What is the approximate threshold for nacelle temperature indication displayed on the ECAM?

options.a: It is displayed when at or above 150°C
options.b: It is displayed when at or above 320°C

justification: (diagram) states: 'NACELLE TEMPERATURE INDICATION (DISPLAYED IF ONE NACELLE TEMPERATURE IS AT OR ABOVE 320°C)'.

question: Where is the nacelle temperature sensor physically mounted?

options.a: At the 6 o'clock position on the fan case
options.b: In the nacelle core zone ventilation air exit

justification: States: 'A temperature probe installed in the nacelle core zone ventilation air exit monitors the nacelle temperature.'

question: Which zone includes the engine core compartments?
justification: States: 'Zone 2: core compartment ventilation...'

question: What are the four primary thrust limit modes displayed on the upper ECAM?
justification: Lists the thrust limit modes as: CL, FLX, MCT, and TOGA.

question: In manual thrust mode, what determines the Engine Pressure Ratio (EPR) command?
justification: And 273 state that in manual mode, the EPR command corresponds to the Throttle Resolver Angle (TRA).

question: If the throttle levers are set between two detent points, which detent determines the thrust limit mode?

options.c: The mode is ignored until a detent is reached

justification: States: 'If the throttle levers are set between two detent points, the upper detent will determine the thrust limit mode.'

question: When is 'Approach Idle' obtained by the FADEC?

options.a: When the engine is in CRANK mode
options.c: During all flight phases above 10,000 ft

justification: States: 'Approach idle is obtained when the slats are extended.'

question: What is the Engine Pressure Ratio (EPR) a ratio of?

options.b: P4.9 (LP turbine exhaust) to P2 (engine inlet) pressure

justification: States: 'The actual EPR is the actual value given by the ratio of the LP turbine exhaust pressure (P4.9) to the engine inlet pressure.'

question: When autothrust is active and the throttle levers are between IDLE and CL, what is the EPR command?
justification: States: 'When engaged, the auto thrust function becomes active... The EPR command is the FMGC EPR target. The auto thrust function is active when the throttle levers are set between IDLE and CL...'

question: In what specific condition does the autothrust function become active automatically and command TOGA thrust?
justification: States: 'NOTE: In alpha floor condition the auto thrust function becomes active automatically. The EPR target is TOGA.'

question: What is the TLA position for the MAX CLIMB detent?
justification: States: '...the MAX CLIMB detent point set to 25 deg.TLA...'

question: If autothrust is engaged on an A320 with only one engine running, what is the active range limit of the throttle lever?
justification: States: 'NOTE: The auto thrust function active range is extended to MCT in the case of single engine operation.'

question: What is the conversion relationship between Throttle Lever Angle (TLA) and Throttle Resolver Angle (TRA)?
justification: And 136 state: '1° of TLA corresponds to 1.9° of TRA.'

question: How many resolvers are contained within the Throttle Control Unit (TCU)?
justification: States: 'The throttle control unit comprises:...-2 resolvers (one resolver per FADEC (ECU/EEC))'.

question: What type of electrical signal does the TCU resolver receive from the FADEC?
justification: States: 'Each resolver... receives its electrical excitation current (6 VAC) from the related FADEC channel...'

question: The TCU input lever drives how many gear sectors?

options.b: Two gear sectors assembled face to face

justification: States: 'The input lever drives two gear sectors assembled face to face.'

question: How many potentiometers are driven by each gear sector in the TCU?
justification: States: 'Each sector drives itself a set of one resolver and three potentiometers.' (Total of 6 as listed earlier in the same page).

question: What is the accuracy of the throttle control unit error between input lever and resolver angle?
justification: States: 'The accuracy of the throttle control unit... is 0.5 deg.TRA.'

question: When the reverse latching lever is pulled up to select reverse power, what occurs at the throttle control lever?

options.a: An electrical signal inhibits the EEC channel B
options.b: An intermediate mechanical stop at 0 deg. TLA is overridden
options.c: The BSBV is commanded to the fully closed position

justification: States: 'An intermediate mechanical stop is set to 0 deg.TLA. This stop is overridden when the reverse latching lever is pulled up for selection of the reverse power.'

question: Which signal from the TCU is dedicated to the Engine Interface Unit (EIU)?
justification: The TCU comprises: '-1 switch whose signal is dedicated to the EIU'.

question: During maintenance, what device is used for rigging the TCU resolver and potentiometers?
justification: Lists: '-A pin device for rigging the resolver and potentiometers'.

question: Where is the Oil Pressure Transmitter (XMTR) located?

options.b: Bolted to a bracket on the top left side of the engine fan case
options.c: Mounted directly on the angle gearbox

justification: States: 'The oil pressure XMTR is bolted to a bracket on the top left side of the engine fan case.'

question: Where is the scavenge oil temperature thermocouple located?

options.a: In the supply line near the pressure pump
options.b: In the combined scavenge line between the master magnetic chip detector and the scavenge filter

justification: States: 'The scavenge oil temperature thermocouple is located in the combined scavenge line between the master magnetic chip detector and the scavenge filter...'

question: At what differential pressure does the oil scavenge filter bypass valve open?
justification: States: 'The by-pass valve opens at 20 PSI.' (While the ECAM is activated at 12 PSI).

question: What is the measured temperature range of the oil temperature resistor unit?
justification: States: 'Temperature measurement range: -60°C to 250°C.'

question: Which bearing compartment scavenge line is monitored by a pressure transducer for correct valve operation?
justification: And 359 state: 'A pressure transducer, installed on this line, monitors the No.4 bearing scavenge pressure.' This is to monitor the correct operation of the No. 4 bearing 2-position scavenge valve.

question: If the engine oil pressure drops below 60 PSI, what happens on the ECAM?

options.a: The indication remains green but starts flashing
options.b: The indication becomes red and a LOP warning is triggered
options.c: The indication disappears and is replaced by 'XX'

justification: States: '...and red if the pressure drops below 60 PSI. The Oil LOW PRESSURE switch sends its discrete signal to the FWC to trigger the LOP warning, when the pressure drops below 60 PSI.'

question: At what oil quantity does the ECAM indication begin flashing green in Advisory mode?
justification: States: 'Normal quantity is indicated in green on the ECAM, flashing green in Advisory mode if oil quantity is lower than 5 Quarts.'

question: What is the ECAM indication behavior if the oil temperature reaches 165°C?

options.c: Amber indication and a high oil temperature warning is triggered

justification: States: 'The indication becomes amber and a high oil temperature warning is triggered, if the oil temperature reaches 165 °C.'

question: What causes the No. 4 bearing scavenge valve to move from its max-flow (open) position to min-flow (closed)?

options.c: Manual override through a square drive

justification: States: 'When this [P10] pressure exceeds 150 psi, the valve moves away from the max flow stop... The valve moves towards the min flow or high power setting.'

question: During engine shutdown, what happens to the No. 4 bearing scavenge valve?

options.a: It is held in the fully closed position by magnets
options.b: It is held spring loaded in the fully open (max-flow) position
options.c: It is bypassed by the anti-siphon restrictor

justification: States: 'In the low-power position... the valve is held spring loaded in the fully open position.' At shutdown, P10 is gone, so the spring holds it open.

question: What type of thrust reverser system is used on the IAE V2500?
justification: States: 'The thrust reverser system is of the aerodynamic blockage type.'

question: Which hydraulic systems supply power to the thrust reverser actuators for engines 1 and 2 respectively?

options.a: Green for engine 1, Yellow for engine 2
options.b: Blue for engine 1, Green for engine 2
options.c: Yellow for engine 1, Blue for engine 2

justification: States: 'The hydraulic power required... is supplied by: - green system for engine 1, - yellow system for engine 2.'

question: How are the four hydraulic actuators on each reverser half synchronized?

options.a: By an electrical pulse-width modulation system from the EEC
options.b: By flexible drive shafts inside the deploy hydraulic lines
options.c: By mechanical geared racks along the 'C' duct inner wall

justification: States: 'The operation of the actuators is synchronized by flexible drive shafts inside the deploy hydraulic lines, i.e. the synchronizing system.'

question: What component within the HCU is operated specifically to 'deploy only'?
justification: States: 'The directional valve is operated to deploy only.'

question: Where are the internal locks for the translating sleeves located?
justification: And 339 clarify that 'Internal locks in the lower actuators are hydraulically operated' and 'mechanical locks, which are an integral part of the lower actuators.'

question: What 'third defense line' component must be opened by the Spoiler Elevator Computers (SECs) before the HCU is supplied with hydraulic pressure?
justification: States: 'For third defense line purposes, the Spoiler Elevator Computers (SECs) have previously opened the SOV and the hydraulic pressure is supplied to the HCU.'

question: To command thrust reverser deployment, the EEC requires an 'aircraft on ground' signal from the:
justification: States: 'To command the thrust reverser, the EEC needs an "aircraft on ground" signal supplied by the Landing Gear Control and Interface Units (LGCIUs).'

question: During the deploy sequence, what indicates to the EEC that hydraulic pressure downstream of the isolation valve is sufficient?
justification: States: 'The pressure switch provides signals to the EEC to indicate that the hydraulic pressure downstream of the isolation valve is sufficient.'

question: After the translating sleeves reach the fully stowed position, how long does the EEC wait before de-energizing the isolation valve to ensure full lock engagement?
justification: States: 'The EEC will de-energize the isolation valve 5 seconds after the translating sleeves reach the fully stowed position to ensure full lock engagement.'

question: What is the cockpit indication for the thrust reverser during transition (in transit)?
justification: States: 'An amber REVerse indication appears when the translating sleeves are in transit and then becomes green when the sleeves are deployed.'

question: What is the first step in deactivating the Thrust Reverser HCU according to the maintenance procedure?

options.a: Remove the lockout pin from the translating sleeve
options.b: Move the inhibition lever to the OFF position and insert the quick release pin

justification: States: 'Deactivate the Thrust Reverser HCU by removing the quick release pin... Move the inhibition lever to the OFF position and insert the quick release pin.'

question: For easy identification of a deactivated thrust reverser, what color is the lockout pin that stands out of the structure?
justification: States: 'NOTE: Note: For easy identification of a deactivated thrust reverser, the red colored lockout pin will stand out...'

question: If a thrust reverser cannot be repaired before the next flight, what is the required configuration for dispatch?

options.c: Hydraulically isolated but with pins removed

justification: States: 'Deactivation and lockout are therefore provided to secure the translating sleeves in stowed position when the aircraft has to be dispatched...'

question: What must be applied to the threads of the lockout pin and plug before installation during deactivation?
justification: States: 'Make sure that the lockout pin and the plug are cleaned and that anti seize material is applied to the threads of both components...'

question: After installing the lockout pins, what check must be performed using the ECAM?

options.a: Ensure the oil level is in the green band
options.b: Ensure the green or amber REV indication does not appear in the EPR indication during the test
options.c: Check that N2 reaches 20% within 10 seconds

justification: States: 'During the test make sure that the green or amber REV indication does not appear in the EPR indication...'

question: What warning is issued regarding working on the engine or thrust reverser system?

options.a: The system must be pressurized to 450 PSI
options.b: The system must be deactivated using the HCU lever to prevent accidental operation
options.c: The IDG must be removed first

justification: And 371 give the warning: 'THE THRUST REVERSER SYSTEM SHOULD BE DEACTIVATED USING THE HYDRAULIC CONTROL UNIT (HCU) LEVER, BEFORE WORKING ON THE SYSTEM OR ON THE ENGINE.'

question: To complete the deactivation procedure after HCU inhibition, where must the lockout pins be installed?

options.b: In the lockout assembly on the outside of each translating sleeve
options.c: Inside the pylon access panel A

justification: States: 'Install the lockout pin in the lockout assembly of the translating sleeve.'

question: When performing the operational test of the thrust reverser system with CFDS after lockout, what does the CFDIU simulate?
justification: And 371 state: 'In this case the Centralized Fault Display Unit (CFDIU) simulates an engine running, i.e. the N2 condition, to permit the thrust reverser deployment [test].'

question: What is the final step in the cockpit after completing the TR deactivation for flight operation?

options.a: Switch the EEC mode to N1
options.b: Install a warning notice to show that the thrust reverser is inoperative and make a logbook entry

justification: States: 'In the cockpit install a warning notice to show that the thrust reverser is inoperative. Make an entry in the logbook. This completes the Thrust Reverser deactivation...'

question: Which ECAM warning should NOT be displayed after a successful TR deactivation procedure and aircraft reconfiguration?
justification: States: 'Check that the ECAM warning ENG 1(or 2) Reverse Unlocked is not displayed.'

question: What is the name of the system required on the aircraft pylon to facilitate engine removal and installation?
justification: States: 'The removal and installation of the engine requires the installation of a bootstrap system on the aircraft pylon.'

question: How many trunnions are used to fix the engine to the transportation stand?
justification: States: 'The engine transportation stand... can be fixed to the engine by means of four trunnions.'

question: The bootstrap system is composed of two elements installed at which locations on the pylon?

options.a: On the left and right sides
options.b: At the front and at the rear
options.c: Inside the fan case and at the exhaust

justification: States: 'The bootstrap system is composed of two elements, to be installed at the front and at the rear of the pylon.'

question: What equipment is attached to the ends of the bootstrap system to lower or lift the engine?
justification: States: 'Each element permits to attach at its ends the chain pulley blocks assembly and dynamometers...'

question: Where are the front trunnions for the transportation stand fixed on the engine?

options.a: On the fan case 12 o'clock position
options.b: On the LP compressor case, LH and RH sides
options.c: On the intermediate case top center

justification: States: '...two front trunnions fixed on the LP compressor case, LH side and RH side.'

question: What is a mandatory requirement regarding the engine mount bolts during installation?

options.a: They must be torqued using a power wrench
options.b: Always change them for new or inspected ones; never reuse the same bolts
options.c: Coat the bolts in engine oil before installation

justification: States: 'Note that you never use the same bolts. Always change them for new or inspected ones.'

question: What action must be performed on each FWD engine mount bolt before removal during the engine change process?

options.b: Each bolt is loosened and retorqued to the maximum force an operator using a standard wrench can apply
options.c: Mark the position with red paint

justification: States: 'On the FWD engine mount, each bolt is loosened and retorqued to the maximum force an operator using a standard wrench can apply.' This is likely to break any seizure before lifting.

question: What must be checked on the dynamometers during the initial stage of engine lifting for installation?

options.a: That the pressure is exactly 3000 PSI
options.b: That they show the correct load
options.c: That the pointers are at zero

justification: States: 'Start the lifting using the pulley levers and check that the dynamometers show the correct load.'

question: What precaution is given during the descent of the engine during removal?

options.a: Avoid any dynamic effect during descent
options.b: Ensure the oil tank is at the 'FULL' mark
options.c: Keep the IDG cables connected until the engine reaches the trolley

justification: (NOTE) states: 'Avoid any dynamic effect during descent.' and 'Slowly continue the descent...'

question: What safety equipment must be available before starting any task on the fuel system during engine removal?
justification: States: 'WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT YOU HAVE THE CORRECT FIRE FIGHTING EQUIPMENT AVAILABLE BEFORE YOU START ANY TASK ON THE FUEL SYSTEM.'

question: What is the weight of the V2500 fan module assembly?
justification: States: 'WARNING: BE CAREFUL DURING THE REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION OF THE FAN MODULE, IT WEIGHS APPROXIMATELY 395 LBS (179 KG).'

question: How many curvic coupling bolts attach the fan module to the LP compressor/intermediate case module?
justification: States: 'There are twenty-four curvic coupling bolts which attach the fan module to the LP compressor/intermediate case module.'

question: What is the correct procedure for tightening the fan module curvic coupling bolts?

options.a: Use a power wrench at high speed
options.b: The torque value must always be on the increase
options.c: Tighten all bolts simultaneously using a hydraulic ring

justification: States: 'When you torque the curvic coupling bolts, it is important that the torque value is on the increase. A new bolt must be installed if the torque value is constant or decreases.'

question: During fan module removal, how many bolts must remain in position until after the support and slinging tools are installed?
justification: States: 'During removal of the fan module, keep three of the bolts in position until after the installation of the support and slinging tools.'

question: Which markings are used to align the fan disk during installation?

options.b: The correlation mark and the U slot of the stub shaft
options.c: The RED marks on the master chip detector

justification: States: 'Use the correlation mark and the U slot of the stub shaft to align the fan disk.'

question: What warning is given regarding handling the fan blades?

options.a: They are balanced with mercury and should not be tilted
options.b: The leading edges can cause injury; use approved gloves
options.c: They must be kept at a temperature of 120°F

justification: States: 'THE LEADING EDGES OF THE FAN BLADES CAN CAUSE INJURY TO YOUR HANDS. PUT APPROVED GLOVES ON YOUR HANDS...'

question: During fan blade replacement, what must be verified to ensure engine balance?

options.a: The blade must have the same moment weight
options.b: The blade must be from the same manufacturing batch
options.c: The blade must be installed at the 6 o'clock position

justification: States: '...in this case, the fan blade must be changed with the same moment weight.'

question: Where is the moment weight of the fan blade identified?

options.b: On the bottom face of the blade root
options.c: Engraved on the front blade retaining ring

justification: States: 'NOTE: Note that the moment weight of the fan blade is identified on the bottom face of the blade root.'

question: How is the front blade retaining ring released from the stage one fan disk?

options.b: By installing puller bolts at six hole positions and tightening them
options.c: By removing the 56 bolts on the common nozzle assembly

justification: States: 'Next, install puller bolts at six hole positions, and tighten them. Using these puller bolts, release the front blade retaining ring...'

question: What must NOT be done when tightening the fan module curvic coupling bolts?

options.a: Use a standard manual torque wrench
options.c: Perform a minimum idle check afterward

justification: States: 'Do not use a power wrench to tighten the bolts. The use of a power wrench can cause damage to the bolts.'

question: What is the recommended timeframe for checking and servicing engine oil after shutdown?
justification: States: 'NOTE: Note: If possible, the engine oil should be checked and serviced within 5 to 60 minutes after shutdown.'

question: If the engine has been shut down for more than 1 hour but less than 10 hours, what is required before servicing?

options.b: Start the engine and run at idle for 3 minutes

justification: States: 'Note: If the engine has been shutdown more 1 hour but less than 10 hours, start the engine and run at idle for 3 minutes prior to servicing.'

question: What is the consequence of opening the oil filler cap immediately after shutdown without waiting 5 minutes?

options.a: The EEC will trigger a false LOP warning
options.b: Residual pressure in the tank can cause hot oil to spray out and burn the technician
options.c: The oil quantity transmitter will lose its calibration

justification: Warns: 'CAUTION: Caution: The engine should be shut down for at least 5 minutes prior to oil servicing... If you open the filler cap when there is pressure in the tank the hot oil can spray out and burn you.'

question: If the engine has been shut down for 10 hours or more, what sequence must be followed to ensure the oil level shown is correct?

options.a: Add oil until the sight gage is full, then run the engine
options.b: Dry crank, then engine start and idle run of at least 3 minutes
options.c: Apply 450 PSI of pressure to the oil filler port

justification: States: 'Note: If the engine has been shut down for 10 hours or more, you must dry crank the engine followed by an engine start and idle run of at least 3 minutes duration.'

question: Where is the Master Magnetic Chip Detector (MCD) located?

options.b: On the oil scavenge filter housing attached to the oil tank
options.c: In the combined scavenge line near the de-oiler

justification: States: 'The Master Magnetic Chip Detector (MCD) is located on the oil scavenge filter housing attached to the oil tank.'

question: During maintenance, what must be done if contamination is found on the Master MCD?

options.c: Reset the EEC via the overhead panel

justification: States: 'Note: CONTAMINATION on Master MCD - Inspect ALL other MCD's.'

question: How is the Master MCD plug removed from its housing?

options.a: Pull directly outward after releasing a latch
options.b: Push in and turn the MCD plug counterclockwise

justification: States: '- push in and turn the MCD plug counterclockwise'.

question: What must be checked regarding the markings when re-installing the Master MCD?

options.a: Check that the RED marks are aligned
options.c: Check that the pointer is at the 12 o'clock position

justification: States: '- replace seal ring and re-install - check that the RED marks are aligned.'

question: Which of these is NOT a location for an additional chip detector on the V2500?
justification: The diagram shows chip detectors for: Gearbox LH/RH, No. 5 Bearing, Angle Gearbox, No. 1, 2, 3 Bearing, and De-Oiler. There is no chip detector on the inlet cowl lip.

question: What is the purpose of the additional magnetic chip detectors in the oil system?

options.a: To provide extra cooling for the scavenging line
options.b: To isolate the source of metallic debris
options.c: To sense the pressure at station 4.9

justification: States: 'Additional magnetic chip detectors are installed in the oil system to isolate the source of metallic debris.'

question: In which engine structure is the forward sump cavity located?
justification: According to the manual (), the forward sump is located in the fan frame and contains bearings No. 1, No. 2, and No. 3.

question: Which specific bearing is installed between the HPT rear shaft and the LPT shaft to take radial loads?
justification: The No. 4 bearing is a roller bearing installed between the HPT rear shaft and the LPT shaft to take HPT rotor radial loads ().

question: Besides supporting rotors, what forces must the engine bearings control during aircraft maneuvers?

options.a: Aerodynamic stall loads and thermal expansion

justification: The manual states the bearings must control the forces of gravity weight, aerodynamic loads of pumping and turbine driving, and gyroscopic loads due to maneuvers ().

question: What is used to minimize oil consumption by ensuring oil is retained within the circuit at the sumps?
justification: The sumps are sealed with labyrinth type oil seals which must be pressurized to ensure oil is retained and consumption is minimized ().

question: From where is the air used for seal pressurization extracted?
justification: Pressurization air is extracted from the primary airflow at the booster discharge and injected between the two labyrinth seals ().

question: What happens to the pressurization air once it enters the oil sump cavity?

options.a: It is ducted to the stage 4 bleed valve
options.b: It is directed to an air/oil rotating separator
options.c: It is used to cool the HPT shroud support

justification: Once inside the oil sump cavity, the pressurization air is directed to an air/oil rotating separator and then out through the center vent tube ().

question: Through which components does vented air exit the engine from the sump cavity?

options.a: Variable bleed valves and fan exhaust
options.b: Center vent tube, rear extension duct, and flame arrestor
options.c: IDG oil cooler and overboard drain mast

justification: The air/oil rotating separator directs air out of the engine via the center vent tube, rear extension duct, and flame arrestor ().

question: What is the function of the cavity between the two labyrinth seals?

options.a: To collect any oil that crosses the seal and route it to drain pipes
options.b: To provide high-pressure air for the turbine clearance control
options.c: To house the magnetic chip detector probes

justification: The manual states any oil that might cross the oil seal is collected in a cavity between the seals and routed to drain pipes ().

question: Which module supports the transfer and accessory gearboxes and contains the forward mount?
justification: The fan frame module carries inlet cowl loads, supports the gearboxes, and contains the forward mount ().

question: What is the purpose of the Outlet Guide Vanes (OGVs) located before the combustion chamber?

options.a: To increase air velocity for combustion
options.b: To redirect the airflow before it enters the chamber
options.c: To filter debris from the primary flow

justification: Before entering the combustion chamber, the last stator vanes (OGVs) must redirect the airflow ().

question: How many stages of the 9 HPC stator stages are variable?

options.a: The IGVs and the first 3 stages

justification: The manual states the IGVs and the stator vanes of the following 3 stages are variable (VSVs) ().

question: Which systems are used to optimize the stall margin and prevent compressor surge?

options.a: The EGT probes and fuel flow transmitter
options.b: The VSVs and variable bleed valves
options.c: The chip detectors and oil relief valve

justification: To prevent compressor surge, stall effects are controlled using Variable Stator Vanes (VSVs) and variable bleed valves ().

question: According to the manual, when is the compressor said to be surging?

options.a: When N1 exceeds the rating limit by 10%
options.b: When the compressor is incapable of compressing the airflow
options.c: When the chip detector pop-out indicator is extended

justification: The manual defines surge as the condition when the compressor is incapable of compressing the airflow ().

question: How is a 'Stall' described in relation to compressor operation?

options.a: A global failure of the turbine shaft
options.b: A local effect where the airflow is not compressed
options.c: An automatic shutdown of the FADEC system

justification: Stall is defined as a local effect where the airflow is not compressed, which can bring the compressor to surge ().

question: Where does the mechanical energy that the turbine provides to the compressor shaft transmit to?

options.a: The accessory gearbox through the radial shaft
options.b: The airflow via the compressor blades
options.c: The pylon through the forward mount

justification: The mechanical energy provided by the turbine to the compressor shaft is transmitted to the airflow with the compressor blades ().

question: What is the natural tendency of the airflow due to the compression ratio within the engine?

options.a: To expand in a counter direction
options.b: To cool down immediately before combustion
options.c: To bypass the core through the TR ducts

justification: The manual states that due to the compression ratio, the airflow tries to expand in a counter direction ().

question: What improvement was introduced by TECH INSERTION technology regarding the HPC?

options.b: Re-designed HPC rotor blades to improve efficiency
options.c: Replacement of VSVs with fixed stators

justification: TECH INSERTION technology introduces re-designed HPC rotor blades to improve HPC efficiency ().

question: Which component is included in the combustion case to reduce sensitivity to the compressor air velocity profile?
justification: The case includes a diffuser for the reduction of combustion chamber sensitivity to the compressor air velocity profile ().

question: How is the air flow divided at the combustion chamber?

options.a: Into primary and secondary bypass flow
options.b: Into flow that goes through the chamber and flow that encircles it
options.c: Into lubrication supply and scavenge flow

justification: The manual states the flow is divided into the flow that goes through the combustion chamber and the flow that encircles it ().

question: What is the purpose of the air flow that encircles the combustion chamber?

options.a: To supply fuel to the nozzles
options.b: To provide film cooling to the first turbine nozzle
options.c: To drive the LP turbine rotor

justification: The flow that encircles the chamber provides film cooling to the first turbine nozzle and reduces gas temperature at the turbine inlet ().

question: At what point does the combustion process finish?

options.c: After the 4th stage of the LPT

justification: The combustion process finishes before entering the HPT nozzles ().

question: What happens to the velocity of HP gases as they pass through the diffuser?

options.b: The velocity decreases before entering the chamber
options.c: The velocity remains constant while pressure increases

justification: HP gases pass through the OGVs then in the diffuser decrease their velocity and enter the combustion chamber ().

question: Which regulation standards are met by the modified dilution and improved cooling profile of TECH INSERTION engines?

options.b: Committee on Aviation Environmental Protection (CAEP) 6th meeting

justification: TECH INSERTION introduces modified dilution/cooling to reduce NOx emissions and meet CAEP 6th meeting requirements ().

question: When does the combustion process start?

options.a: When fuel hits the diffuser walls
options.b: When the mixture encounters the burning zones
options.c: When N1 reaches 16% during manual start

justification: The manual states when the mixture encounters the burning zones, the combustion process starts ().

question: Where does the flow that enters the combustion chamber go first in a Single Annular Combustor engine?

options.b: Through the dome to cool its surface
options.c: Directly into the HPT rotor blades

justification: The flow that enters the chamber goes first through the dome and cools its surface ().

question: What is the benefit of the new HPT blades introduced by TECH INSERTION technology?

options.a: Lower aerodynamic loss between HPT and LPT
options.b: Elimination of the need for EGT monitoring
options.c: Reduction of the number of fuel nozzles to 10

justification: TECH INSERTION introduces new HPT blades with lower aerodynamic loss between HPT and LPT, resulting in reduced fuel burn ().

question: The turbine section is formed by which two modules?
justification: The turbine section consists of the HPT module and the LPT module ().

question: How many stages are in the LPT module nozzle and rotor?
justification: The LPT module consists of 4-stage nozzle and rotor ().

question: What is the description of the HPT nozzle assembly?
justification: The HPT nozzle is a single-stage air-cooled assembly that mounts in the combustion case ().

question: Which stages are included in the LPT nozzle assemblies of the LPT stator assembly?
justification: The LPT stator assembly consists of the LPT case and stages 2-4 nozzle assemblies ().

question: To what structure is the turbine frame bolted?
justification: The turbine frame is bolted to the LPT case and supports the primary exhaust nozzle ().

question: How is the HPT rotor assembly characterized?
justification: The HPT rotor is a single-stage, air-cooled, high-efficiency turbine ().

question: Where is the stage 1 LPT nozzle assembly located?
justification: The manual states the HPT shroud and stage 1 LPT nozzle assembly is located inside the combustion case ().

question: Which of these is a component of the LPT rotor assembly?
justification: The LPT rotor assembly is composed of LPT disks, stage 1 blade assembly, rotating air seals, and stages 2-4 ().

question: How is energy transferred from the combustion gases to the turbine rotor?

options.a: The gases cool down and expand the LPT casing
options.b: The gases deliver energy to the turbine blades forcing the rotor to turn
options.c: The gases enter the accessory gearbox to drive the pumps

justification: Energy is delivered to the turbine rotor by gases from the combustion chambers which deliver energy to the blades forcing the rotor to turn ().

question: Where is the hand cranking drive for the N2 shaft provided?

options.a: On the rear face of the accessory gearbox
options.b: On the front face of the accessory gearbox
options.c: Inside the cockpit on the maintenance panel

justification: A hand cranking drive for the N2 shaft is provided on the front face of the accessory gearbox ().

question: What types of line replaceable seals are used for the gearbox gears?

options.c: Teflon O-rings or rubber lip seals

justification: Gears are plug-in units with line replaceable magnetic or spring-loaded carbon seals ().

question: Where is the air starter located in relation to the gearbox?

options.a: On the RH side of the gearbox rear face
options.b: On the LH side of the gearbox front face

justification: The air starter is on the RH side of the gearbox rear face ().

question: What is the purpose of the handcranking drive mentioned in the maintenance practice?

options.a: To manually start the engine in case of starter failure
options.b: To permit manual rotation of the N2 shaft for inspections
options.c: To bleed the fuel pump before dispatch

justification: Hand cranking of the N2 shaft is provided for maintenance purposes such as boroscope inspections or checking for rotation ().

question: Where is the lubrication unit installed?

options.b: On the right-hand side of the AGB front face
options.c: On the aft bulkhead of the pylon

justification: The lubrication unit is installed on the right-hand side of the AGB front face ().

question: On which side of the accessory gearbox is the fuel pump assembly located?
justification: The fuel pump assembly is located on the accessory gearbox LH side ().

question: To which component is the drain collector assembly attached?

options.b: The aft side of the accessory gearbox

justification: The drain collector assembly is attached to the aft side of the accessory gearbox ().

question: Which aerodynamic station corresponds to the Exhaust Gas Temperature (EGT) measuring plane?
justification: The manual identifies STA 49.5 as the EGT measuring plane ().

question: What does aerodynamic station STA 25 represent?
justification: Station STA 25 is the HPC inlet ().

question: Which station represents the interface at the nose cowl inlet?
justification: Station STA 0 is the nose cowl inlet ().

question: Where is the PS12 sensor designed to measure static pressure?
justification: The PS12 sensor measures static pressure from the fan inlet ().

question: Which station is relevant for the measurement of compressor discharge temperature (T3)?
justification: The T3 sensor measures compressor discharge temperature, which is at STA 3 (pages 25, 410).

question: Where can the HPT blade leading edges be inspected during a boroscope task?
justification: The HPT blade leading edges can be inspected through the igniter holes ().

question: How is a boroscope inspection generally realized?

options.b: With an optical tube equipped with a camera
options.c: Using infrared thermal imaging through the exhaust

justification: Boroscope inspections are realized with a rigid or flexible optical tube, generally equipped with a camera for visualization ().

question: What provides the interface between the engine and the aircraft for fluids, electrics, and mechanical forces?
justification: The pylons provide an interface between the engine and the aircraft for electrics, fluids, pneumatics, and mechanical forces ().

question: What is the primary function of the engine nacelle?

options.b: To provide aerodynamic airflow around the engine and protect accessories
options.c: To transfer mechanical torque from the fan to the AGB

justification: The engine is enclosed in a nacelle which provides aerodynamic airflow and ensures protection for the accessories ().

question: Which directions are NOT restrained by the engine aft mount?
justification: The aft mount restrains engine movement in all directions except forward and aft ().

question: Which specific loads are carried by the engine forward mount?

options.a: Engine thrust, vertical, and side loads

justification: The forward mount carries the engine thrust, vertical, and side loads ().

question: How many bolts and self-locking nuts are used to attach the forward mount to the pylon?
justification: The forward mount is attached to the pylon by four bolts and self-locking nuts ().

question: What must be confirmed before removing the engine from the pylon?

options.a: The ENG MASTER control switch is ON
options.b: Slats are retracted and appropriate circuit breakers are open
options.c: The fire extinguisher bottles are discharged

justification: Before engine removal, make sure ENG MASTER is OFF, slats are retracted, and CBs are open ().

question: On which engine side is the fluid disconnect panel located?
justification: Engine interfaces on the engine LH side include the fluid disconnect panel ().

question: Where is the core electrical junction box located?

options.a: On the fan case upper part
options.b: In the zone of the forward mount

justification: The core electrical junction box is located in the zone of the forward mount ().

question: How many elements compose the bootstrap system used for engine removal and installation?

options.a: One element installed at the pylon center
options.b: Two elements, to be installed at the front and at the rear of the pylon
options.c: Four elements, one for each trunnion

justification: The bootstrap system is composed of two elements, to be installed at the front and at the rear of the pylon ().

question: How is the engine transportation stand fixed to the engine?

options.a: By sixteen LP turbine attach rings

justification: The transportation stand can be fixed to the engine by means of four trunnions: two front and two rear ().

question: What is the composition of the inlet cowl inner barrel?
justification: The inlet cowl is composed of an acoustical composite inner barrel, outer barrel, and a nose lip ().

question: How many identical attach fittings are provided for the inlet cowl?
justification: For removal and installation, the inlet cowl is provided with 36 identical attach fittings ().

question: Where does the hot bleed air exhaust after passing through the cowl nose lip for anti-icing?

options.b: Through a flush exit duct in the outer barrel
options.c: Into the fan compartment ventilation zone

justification: The air exhausts overboard through a flush exit duct in the outer barrel ().

question: Through what type of joint are longitudinal and transverse loads distributed into the fan case forward flange?
justification: Loads are distributed into the fan case forward flange through a bolted joint ().

question: What is the structure of the acoustically treated inner barrel in the thrust reverser?

options.b: Aluminum perforated face sheet bonded to aluminum honeycomb core

justification: The inner barrel in the TR is acoustically treated and consists of aluminum perforated face sheet bonded to aluminum honeycomb core ().

question: How many hoist points are provided on the inlet cowl for removal and installation?
justification: The inlet cowl is provided with 4 hoist points for removal and installation ().

question: How is the primary nozzle attached to the LPT frame?

options.c: By a V-groove and J-ring clamp

justification: The primary nozzle is attached to the LPT frame by means of 16 bolts ().

question: What is the function of the centerbody in the exhaust section?

options.a: To redirect bypass air into the primary flow
options.c: To house the T5 temperature sensor

justification: The centerbody provides engine center venting ().

question: What forms the upper firewall of both the fan and core engine compartments?
justification: The pylon floor forms the upper firewall of both the fan and core compartments ().

question: Which component uses fuel as a cooling medium to cool Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) oil?
justification: The manual states fuel is used for cooling for engine oil and Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) oil, specifically through the IDG oil cooler (pages 181, 198).

question: What is the maximum core engine speed (N2) limit set by the overspeed governor system?
justification: The overspeed governor system limits the core engine speed (N2) to a maximum of 106% ().

question: What is the cockpit indication if there is a disagreement between control and position of the HP fuel SOV?

options.a: The N1 indicator circle turns amber
options.b: An ECAM warning is triggered and the engine FAULT light comes on
options.c: The FADEC automatically switches to Channel B

justification: In case of disagreement between control and position of the HPSOV, an ECAM warning is triggered and the engine FAULT light comes on ().

question: For maintenance purposes, how can FADEC power supply be restored on the ground with the engine shut down?

options.a: By setting the MASTER switch to ON
options.b: By using the FADEC GND PWR pushbutton switch on the maintenance panel (50VU)
options.c: By engaging the manual override on the starter SOV

justification: The ENGINE FADEC GrouND PoWeR P/B on the maintenance panel (50VU) permits power restoration on the ground ().

question: How many independent subsystems compose the engine ignition system?
justification: The ignition system is comprised of two independent subsystems ().

question: During an automatic start, at what N2 speed is the ignition exciter energized?
justification: During an automatic start, one of the two ignition exciters is energized when the HP rotor reaches 16% of N2 speed ().
